                    ### Question
                    A 66-year-old man presents with severe respiratory distress. He was diagnosed with pulmonary hypertension secondary to occupational pneumoconiosis. Biopsy findings of the lung showed ferruginous bodies. What is the most likely etiology?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Coal
opb. Iron
opc. Asbestos
opd. Beryllium
ope. Silica

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The presence of ferruginous bodies in the lung biopsy is indicative of asbestos exposure, as these structures are formed from the inhalation of asbestos fibers. Occupational pneumoconiosis typically results from exposure to various inhaled particulates, but the specific finding of ferruginous bodies strongly suggests asbestos-related disease. While pulmonary hypertension can arise from chronic lung disease, the specific association of ferruginous bodies with asbestos makes it the most likely etiology in this case. Therefore, the most likely etiology is asbestos.
